blocks.body: Trenchless sewer repair, also called no-dig sewer repair, fixes a damaged pipe without digging a trench along its full length. Instead of opening up your yard from the house to the street, we work through one or two access points and repair the pipe from the inside or replace it in place. There are two main methods: cured-in-place pipe (CIPP) lining and pipe bursting. Both fix the line underground, so what's above it stays untouched.

blocks.h2: A Trenchless Repair in a Skokie Yard
blocks.body: Skokie lots are often modest, with the line running under a front lawn, a driveway or both. On lining day, we clean the line, run the camera, install the liner from a cleanout or small opening and let it cure. Then we reopen any branch connections and record the finished pipe. Most homeowners have their plumbing back by evening.

blocks.h2: Trenchless Sewer Questions From Skokie Homeowners

items.q: Can a 1950s clay sewer be lined?
items.answer: Often. If the camera shows the clay is cracked but still holding its shape, it can be lined. Collapsed spots get fixed first.

items.q: How long will a liner last?
items.answer: Liners are designed to last for decades, and the lined section has no joints for roots to enter.

items.q: Will I need a new cleanout?
items.answer: Sometimes. If your line has no good access point, we may add a cleanout, which also makes future service easier.

items.q: How long does the work take?
items.answer: Many Skokie jobs take a day or two, depending on length and method.

items.q: Will lining fix roots for good?
items.answer: Yes, in the lined section. Roots can't get through a seamless liner, and we check the ends on camera.

items.q: How much does trenchless sewer repair cost in Skokie?
items.preview: It depends on length, depth and method. You'll approve a flat price first.
items.answer: It depends on how much of the line needs work, the depth, the method and access. You'll approve a flat-rate price before we start.
